items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1960-04-30
items.q: So now my first job I played with, with Kidore and his band was a place they called the Palm Garden.

ctx.x: And you were going to tell about when you joined Kidore.

Yeah, I played in his drummer's place, in Henry Martin's place. Henry Martin was playing out at a place on the, at West End, they call it the Bungalow. I guess you heard of that nightclub, the Bungalow. Well, on Sunday nights, Saturdays and Sundays, that was his busy night out there. He couldn't get off, you see. So after we heard me play with Tick Chambers, well, he said, well, let's try. When it's Kelly, he boosts me up, you know, so I was going to make a good drummer and give him a try. I said, he's a good…

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-10-13
items.q: Oh, some time I played with Oryx when he was here, you know what I'm saying?

ctx.x: Such as? How did that work? What you mean? Such as? Who were some of the bands? Oh, some of the bands I'd play with? Yeah, when you were with somebody else.

Oh, some time I played with Oryx when he was here, you know what I'm saying? And I was playing with Pierron and any other band at Warhammer like, oh, several of those bands rock. I played with Rennie, played with Rennie, played with Chris. Mm-hmm. Mm-hmm. And several others. Jack Carey. Mm-hmm. Played with him. Phillip Nixon, Silver Leaf Band. Who was in that band? Who was in that band?
Yeah, he played with him. Oh, he had... Who did you play with? Yeah. Yeah.

items.title: Alfred Williams Interview, 1961-02-03
items.q: Well Joe Oliver went with Ory's band at that time.

ctx.x: Kind of skipping around a little bit. Did you ever work at Pete Lawrence? Yeah, I worked at Pete Lawrence.

When he was at Murray and Iterville. Yeah, I worked there. When I worked there in 19, about 17, 16, I believe in part of 17. How I come to work there, Joe Oliver had the job. Well Joe Oliver went with Ory's band at that time. See, now like Saturday nights and Sunday nights he played with Ory. Well he put me down there, Steve Lewis, Lewis Armstrong, Morris French, you heard of Morris French. Old man Valto, you heard of him, was playing violin. And who was on piano? Well Steve, I told you Steve was on piano. Must…
Well who was in Joe Oliver's band when he was at Pete Lawrence? Old man Valto, he was playing violin.

items.title: Edward "Kid" Ory Interview, 1957-04-20
items.q: So who'd you get? Papa Michael. And who else? I was born in Alfred William Drum and Manuel Mineta.

ctx.x: Oh, yeah? When you got the job, did you send for a band? It's all right. You can talk. No, you can talk. You can sit down. You can sit back.

Why I sent for a band? I sent for Louie and... Louie? Yeah. Louie went back to New Orleans at the time. Oh. And by the time my telegram got there, he had just left. For Chicago? Mm-hmm. Went with you. So who'd you get? Papa Michael. And who else? I was born in Alfred William Drum and Manuel Mineta. And I was three. Oh, and Wade Whaley. Clarence. You know. Yes, I know.
